entries.summary: No verified material change from the 22:39 EST assessment. Thursday's Nasdaq -0.39%, SOX -0.54%, NVDA -4.34%, AMD +5.86% and AVGO +5.54% cash closes remain the latest matched session evidence. October PPI is still pending at 08:30 EST Friday November 13; 6.6% year-over-year is a consensus forecast, not a released result. Open Watch remains 159 curated events, updated 2026-11-12T23:58:32+00:00. Fresh synchronized overnight QQQ/SOX, VXN/VIX, breadth, matched Treasury yields, oil and CME FedWatch observations were not verified.
bullish: Nasdaq closed -0.39% after opening -1.47%, showing substantial absorption of the initial Nvidia shock.
AMD +5.86% and AVGO +5.54% at Thursday's close indicate selective chip rotation rather than uniform sector capitulation.
Foxconn and Siemens data-center demand signals remain supportive of longer-run AI infrastructure spending; no attributable index response is established.

Applied Materials fiscal Q4 adjusted EPS $4.16 versus $4.06 expected and revenue $10.41B versus $10.3B; next-quarter guidance above estimates. Cisco reported adjusted EPS $1.40 versus $1.33 expected, revenue $18.5B versus $18.1B and raised outlook; positive AI networking demand evidence, not proof of Friday market response.
bearish: Nvidia closed -4.34% following the confirmed CEO transition, and SOX finished -0.54%; leadership and semiconductor benchmark remain vulnerable.
Higher oil and long yields reported earlier remain valuation risks, but current synchronized oil/yield measurements are missing.
Reuters reports at least a 25bp December Fed hike fully priced, with a 15% chance of a 50bp move; hotter PPI could worsen duration-sensitive equity pressure.
Applied Materials was reportedly nearly flat after hours despite its beat after falling 3.6% in regular trade; a strong report alone has not confirmed sector-wide risk appetite.

editorial.marketOverview: The last verified US cash session remains Thursday's Nasdaq -0.39%, SOX -0.54%, NVDA -4.34%, AMD +5.86% and AVGO +5.54%. The recovery from intraday weakness and chip-stock dispersion argue against declaring a uniform sector collapse. Positive Cisco and Applied Materials results support underlying AI infrastructure spending, but Friday's market response is not yet known. No fresh synchronized overnight quote set warrants changing the bearish skew.
editorial.whatChanged: The latest check found no new curated Open Watch event and no confirmed post-Thursday market reaction that alters the outlook. Friday's October PPI remains scheduled for 08:30 EST; the reported 6.6% year-over-year consensus is an expectation, not an outcome. The previous assessment's historical oil and Treasury observations remain stale.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Leadership fragility in NVDA, a negative SOX close, inflation sensitivity and higher-rate risk continue to outweigh constructive AMD/AVGO rotation and AI infrastructure earnings. A headline earnings beat is not equivalent to index confirmation. The direction of matched Treasury yields, volatility, breadth and semiconductor leadership after PPI is more diagnostic than an unsynchronized premarket quotation.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday November 13: compare actual October PPI with expectations after 08:30 EST, then assess matched QQQ, SOX, NVDA, 2Y/10Y yields, VXN/VIX and breadth. Monday November 16: test whether semiconductor rotation becomes broad participation or fades. Tuesday November 17: require follow-through before concluding that the bearish near-term regime has changed. These are conditional pathways, not precise price targets.
editorial.bullCase: A benign PPI release followed by falling matched yields, NVDA stabilization, SOX outperforming QQQ and improving breadth would suggest the Thursday shock was absorbed. AMD and AVGO strength and Cisco/AMAT demand signals offer support, but their effect on the index remains unconfirmed until trading resumes.
editorial.bearCase: A hotter-than-expected PPI accompanied by rising yields, renewed NVDA and SOX losses, weaker breadth and higher VXN/VIX would increase the likelihood of another Nasdaq downside leg. Oil would amplify the inflation channel only if contemporaneous Brent/WTI prices verify that pressure.
editorial.watchNext: Verify the official BLS PPI at 08:30 EST Friday, then capture synchronized QQQ/Nasdaq, SOX, NVDA/AMD/AVGO/AMAT/CSCO, Treasury 2Y/10Y, VXN/VIX, advance-decline breadth, Brent/WTI and Fed futures. Check Open Watch for newly curated events and distinguish projected catalyst impacts from actual price responses.
